facts.title: llm-anthropic 0.26
facts.event_hint: llm-anthropic 0.26 adds Claude 5 model entries, server-side tools, typed streaming events, and revised thinking controls
facts.problem: The release addresses integration gaps for newer Claude models, server-side tool invocation, typed streaming of reasoning/tool events, and configurable extended-thinking controls in the LLM CLI/Python interface.
facts.mechanism: The plugin adds Claude Fable 5, Sonnet 5, and Opus 5 model support; exposes WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, and AnthropicMCP through -T or tools=; upgrades to llm>=0.32 for typed event streaming; and replaces legacy thinking options with thinking/thinking_effort controls.

evidence.claim: The release adds Claude Fable 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Opus 5 model entries.
Server-side WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, and AnthropicMCP tools are exposed through the -T interface or Python tools=; prior web_search* output options were removed.
The plugin upgrades to llm>=0.32, where reasoning, tool calls, tool results, and server-side tool results stream as typed events.
Extended thinking is configured with thinking and thinking_effort; thinking_effort accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, or max.

facts.evaluation_context: The source is a Simon Willison weblog release note dated 4 August 2026, describing llm-anthropic 0.26 and its LLM 0.32 integration; it reports no benchmark or deployment measurements.
facts.limitations: This is a secondary release note, not the upstream repository release page. It provides feature claims but no compatibility matrix, performance measurements, failure behavior, or security analysis; upstream primary-source verification remains required.
facts.project_relevance: Typed tool-event streaming and first-class server-side tools may simplify observability and execution routing in an Agent tool chain; verify upstream release details before relying on exact option names or model availability.
source_notes: Evidence is limited to the fetched Simon Willison release note; no primary repository or package metadata was read.
No latency or quality claims were inferred from the feature list.
